name: D.R. Horton
description: D.R. Horton is the largest US homebuilder by homes closed (84,863 in fiscal 2025, at an average price of $370,400) with operating divisions in 126 markets across 36 states. It buys and develops land, builds houses mostly on a spec-and-order basis, and sells them to individual buyers, with a brand range from entry-level to more expensive homes. Around it sit four smaller money makers: a majority-owned (62%) lot developer, Forestar, that sells finished lots largely to Horton itself; a rental business that builds single-family and apartment communities and sells them in bulk to investors; a mortgage and title arm (DHI Mortgage) that finances Horton's own buyers; and other activities. Homebuilding produces about 92 percent of revenue and about 87 percent of pre-tax income. Earnings depend on mortgage rates, home prices and incentives, and land and lumber costs; FY2025 pre-tax income fell to $4.7B from $6.3B.

businessLines.name: Homebuilding
businessLines.how: Individual homebuyers pay the full price at closing (one-time, about $370,000 per home), typically one to three months after signing a contract, most financed by a mortgage; profit is the sale price minus land, construction and selling cost. Driven by mortgage affordability, incentives and lot costs.
businessLines.description: Builds and sells single-family homes and townhomes in 126 markets across 36 states, in six regions (Northwest, Southwest, South Central, Southeast, East, North).

businessLines.name: Rental
businessLines.how: Builds rental communities, leases them until stabilized, then sells each community to an investor in a bulk transaction; revenue is the sale price of the property and profit is the price minus development cost, so income is lumpy by sale.
businessLines.description: Single-family rental communities (built, leased, then sold in bulk) and multi-family rental (apartment) development.

businessLines.name: Forestar
businessLines.how: Buys raw land, develops it into finished lots and sells lots to homebuilders, primarily D.R. Horton (a large share is intersegment and eliminated) under long-term lot purchase contracts, paid per lot at closing.
businessLines.description: Publicly traded (NYSE: FOR) residential lot developer, 62 percent owned by D.R. Horton at 2025-09-30.
